llm.summary: The skill is generally coherent for reading/sending mail, but a built-in watcher script executes a local 'openclaw' CLI to push alerts (potentially forwarding email contents) and that behavior is not documented in the metadata or required-binaries list — review before installing and supplying credentials.

dimensions.detail: Name/description (IMAP/SMTP email) align with the included Node scripts (imap.js, smtp.js, mail parsing and attachment extraction). The skill logically needs node/npm and IMAP/SMTP credentials stored in a credentials file. Minor mismatch: the registry metadata lists no required env vars or primary credential, but the runtime explicitly requires a credentials file (~/.openclaw/credentials/imap-smtp-email.env) containing IMAP/SMTP secrets.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md and the scripts mostly stay within scope (connecting to IMAP/SMTP, parsing messages, extracting attachments, constrained file I/O). However scripts/email-watch-lite.js calls execFileSync to invoke a local 'openclaw' CLI (default) to send alerts/trigger an agent and build agent arguments that may include analyzed email content. That behavior effectively forwards processed email content to another local tool/channel (e.g., whatsapp) and is not declared in the skill metadata or binary requirements — this is scope creep and could result in unexpected information flow.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No remote download/install spec; project uses standard npm dependencies listed in package.json/package-lock.json. Installing with 'npm install' pulls packages from npm registry (expected for a Node tool). No unusual external download URLs or archive extraction were found.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The tool legitimately needs IMAP/SMTP credentials and exposes a credentials file template. It also requires ALLOWED_READ_DIRS / ALLOWED_WRITE_DIRS to constrain filesystem access (a good control). Concern: those sensitive credentials are not declared as required environment variables in the registry metadata (the code reads them via dotenv from a file), so a user might not realize the skill needs account passwords. The requested scopes (read/write limited to workspace dirs) are proportional to the functionality.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill is not 'always: true' and has no special platform privileges. However, the included email-watch-lite watcher is a long-running/automatable component that, when run, can trigger outbound alerts via the local 'openclaw' CLI. If the agent or a cronjob runs that watcher unattended, it can autonomously forward email analysis results to other channels — combine that with credentials access for higher risk.

dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears to implement an IMAP/SMTP client with local parsing and sensible file-access controls, but review these before installing: 1) Credentials: the tool expects full IMAP/SMTP credentials in ~/.openclaw/credentials/imap-smtp-email.env (and will read them via dotenv). Only provide credentials you trust the code to handle; prefer app-specific passwords or restricted accounts. 2) Watcher behavior: scripts/email-watch-lite.js can call a local 'openclaw' CLI to send alerts and agent messages (potentially containing analyzed email text/attachments). If you do not want email content forwarded automatically, do not run the watcher or audit/modify that code. 3) Binaries: the skill will call external binaries (node, npm) and may call 'openclaw' if you enable the watcher — ensure you understand and trust the local openclaw CLI. 4) Audit: skim the JS files for any additional external network calls or unexpected destinations, and run the skill in an isolated environment (or with test accounts) first. If the author documents and declares the 'openclaw' dependency and the automatic alert behavior up front (or removes it), the risk would be reduced.
llm.findings: [execFileSync_call] unexpected: email-watch-lite.js uses child_process.execFileSync(openclawBin, ...) to call a local 'openclaw' CLI and send alert messages. Using a child process to forward email content is not inherently malicious but is not obvious from the skill metadata and can result in exfiltration to other local/remote systems.
